intro: The second book of the Torah is called Shemot. That means "Names." Its English name is Exodus. It tells how Jacob's family became a people. It tells how they were slaves in Egypt. And it tells how they walked out free.

Jewish families tell this story every spring at Passover. Seven weeks later, at Shavuot, they remember a mountain. The Torah says the people heard ten sayings there. In this unit we learn what the Torah says. We learn what Jewish families do to remember. We do not decide if the story is true. We listen and we learn.
By the end, you will be able to tell the story of baby Moses and the burning bush. You will know why matzah is flat. You will know what the ten sayings are. And you will know what a mitzvah is.
bigQuestion: What does the Torah say about leaving Egypt and the mountain, and how do Jewish families remember it every year?

write.prompt: Draw or tell the story of one night: the night the people left Egypt, or the day at the mountain. Use the Torah's words from Exodus 12 (the flat bread) or Exodus 20 (the ten sayings). Say what the Torah says happened, and say one thing a Jewish family does today to remember it.

title: Moses and the Torah

chapters.title: Out of Egypt: The Passover Story
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the Torah say happened when the people left Egypt, and why do Jewish families tell it every year?

story.title: The Youngest Child Asks
story.kicker: It is the first night of Passover, and the smallest person at the table has the biggest job.
paragraphs: It is spring in Chicago. Sam's family sits at a long table. There is flat bread on a plate. It is called matzah. There is a cup of wine. There is a plate with a green herb and a bitter herb. Sam is the youngest child at the table.
Sam's grandma nods at him. It is time. Sam stands up. He asks, "Why is this night different from all other nights?" Everyone smiles. This is the question the youngest child asks every year.

Sam's uncle opens a small book. It is called the Haggadah. That means "the telling." He says, "Tonight we tell a story from the Torah. Long ago, our people were slaves in Egypt. Then they walked out free."

Sam listens. He hears about a baby in a basket. He hears about a bush on fire. He hears about a king who said no. He hears about a sea that opened. Sam looks at the flat bread. "Why is it flat?" he asks. "Wait," says Grandma. "That is part of the story."
story.think: Why do you think the youngest child gets to ask the big question at the Passover table?

lessons.title: Slaves in Egypt
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob's family grew into a people, and a Pharaoh made them slaves.
reading: The second book of the Torah is called Shemot. That means "Names." Its English name is *Exodus*. It starts with a list of names. They are the sons of Jacob who came to Egypt.
The Torah says the family grew and grew. It became a people. Then a new king ruled Egypt. A king of Egypt is called a *Pharaoh*. The story says this Pharaoh was afraid of the people.
So Pharaoh made them slaves. A slave has to work and cannot leave. The Torah says the people made bricks in the hot sun. Their lives were very hard.

words.d: the English name for Shemot, the second book of the Torah; it means going out
a king of Egypt in the Torah's story

look.title: Two Names for One Book
rows: Sons of Jacob named at the start
look.prompt: Which book of the Torah comes before Exodus? Say its name.

check.q: What does Shemot mean?
check.why: Shemot means "Names." The book starts with the names of Jacob's sons.

check.q: What is a Pharaoh?
check.why: In the Torah's story, the king of Egypt is called a Pharaoh.

check.q: What does the Torah say Pharaoh did to the people?
check.why: The Torah says Pharaoh made the people slaves. They had to make bricks.

lessons.title: A Baby in a Basket
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says a mother hid baby Moses in a basket, and Pharaoh's daughter found him.
reading: The Torah says Pharaoh gave a cruel order about baby boys. One mother hid her baby. She made a *basket* and put him in it. She set it in the river reeds.
The baby's big sister watched from far away. Her name was *Miriam*. Then Pharaoh's daughter came to the river. She saw the basket. She opened it and the baby cried.
Pharaoh's daughter felt sorry for him. Miriam ran up. She said, "I know a woman who can feed him." It was the baby's own mother! Pharaoh's daughter named the baby *Moses*.

words.d: the small boat of reeds that held baby Moses in the Torah's story
Moses's big sister, who watched the basket and later sang by the sea
the baby in the basket, who grew up to lead the people out of Egypt

look.title: Look at the River
look.text: Look at the river. Tall reeds grow at the edge. A small basket floats between them. A girl hides behind the reeds and watches. Then a princess and her helpers walk down to the water. The princess points at the basket.
look.prompt: What do you think the girl behind the reeds is feeling? What is she waiting for?

check.q: Where did the mother put the baby's basket?
check.why: The Torah says she put the basket in the reeds at the edge of the river.

check.q: Who watched the basket from far away?
check.why: Miriam was the baby's big sister. She watched to see what would happen.

check.q: Who does the Torah say found the baby?
check.why: Pharaoh's daughter found the basket and named the baby Moses.

lessons.title: A Bush That Did Not Burn Up
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says God spoke to Moses from a burning bush and sent him back to Egypt.
reading: Moses grew up. He left Egypt and became a shepherd. One day he saw a strange thing. A *bush* was on fire. But the fire did not burn it up.
The Torah says God spoke to Moses from the bush. God told Moses to go back to Egypt. God said to tell Pharaoh to let the people go.
Moses was scared. He said, "Who am I?" The Torah says God told him, "I will be with you." Moses's brother Aaron went with him to help him speak.

words.d: a small tree; in the Torah's story, God spoke to Moses from a bush on fire

look.title: The Bush on Fire
look.text: the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
look.prompt: "Consumed" means burned up. What was strange about this fire?

check.q: What was strange about the bush?
choices: It burned but did not burn up
check.why: The Torah says the bush was on fire, but the fire did not burn it up.

check.q: What did God tell Moses to do, in the story?
check.why: The Torah says God sent Moses back to Egypt to tell Pharaoh to let the people go.

check.q: Who went with Moses to help him speak?
check.why: Aaron was Moses's brother. The Torah says he went along to help Moses speak.

lessons.title: Pharaoh Says No
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Moses told Pharaoh to let the people go, and ten plagues came when he said no.
reading: Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh. They said, "Let my people go." Pharaoh said no. He made the people work even harder.

The Torah says ten *plagues* came to Egypt. A plague is a big trouble. The river turned red. Frogs hopped everywhere. Bugs came. Animals got sick. Hail fell. Locusts ate the plants. The sky went dark.
After each plague, Moses asked again. Pharaoh still said no. The last plague was the saddest of all. Then, the Torah says, Pharaoh finally said, "Go."

words.d: a big trouble; the Torah tells of ten plagues that came to Egypt

look.title: Four Small Words
look.text: Let My people go, that they may hold a feast unto Me in the wilderness.
look.prompt: Who is talking to Pharaoh here, and who is the message from?

check.q: What did Moses and Aaron say to Pharaoh?
check.why: The Torah says Moses and Aaron told Pharaoh, "Let my people go."

check.q: How many plagues does the Torah say came to Egypt?
check.why: The Torah tells of ten plagues. Frogs and darkness were two of them.

check.q: What is a plague?
check.why: A plague is a big trouble. The river turning red was one plague.

lessons.title: Bread With No Time to Rise
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the people left Egypt so fast their bread had no time to rise; Jewish families eat matzah to remember.
reading: The Torah says the people left Egypt at night. They had to hurry. Their bread dough had no time to rise. So it baked flat. Flat bread like this is called *matzah*.
That night is called *Passover*. In Hebrew it is Pesach. The Torah says the people put a mark on their doors. The last plague passed over their homes.
Every spring, Jewish families eat matzah for a week. They do this to remember. Flat bread means "we left in a hurry."

words.d: flat bread with no time to rise; Jewish families eat it at Passover
the spring holiday when Jewish families remember leaving Egypt

look.title: Two Kinds of Bread
look.text: Look at two plates. On one plate is a tall, soft loaf of bread. It took hours to rise. On the other plate is matzah. It is flat and crisp, with little holes. It baked in a few minutes.
look.prompt: Which bread would you take if you had to leave right now? Why does the Passover table have that one?

check.q: Why was the bread flat?
choices: It had no time to rise
It got wet in the sea
check.why: The Torah says the people left in a hurry. Their dough had no time to rise.

check.q: What is flat bread with no time to rise called?
check.why: Matzah is the flat bread. Challah is the braided bread for Shabbat.

check.q: When do Jewish families eat matzah for a week?
check.why: At Passover, Jewish families eat matzah to remember leaving Egypt.

lessons.title: The Sea Opens
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the sea opened, the people crossed, and Miriam led the singing.
reading: The people walked out of Egypt. They came to the edge of a *sea*. Then they looked back. Pharaoh had changed his mind. His army was coming.
The Torah says Moses held out his hand. A strong wind blew all night. The sea split in two. There was a dry path in the middle. The people walked across.
On the other side, they were safe. Moses and the people sang a song. Miriam took a drum. The women danced with her. They sang about the sea.

words.d: a very big body of water; the Torah says the sea opened so the people could cross

look.title: Miriam's Song
look.text: Sing ye to the LORD, for He is highly exalted: the horse and his rider hath He thrown into the sea.
look.prompt: Miriam sings this with a drum. What just happened that made her want to sing?

check.q: What does the Torah say happened at the sea?
choices: It split and made a dry path
check.why: The Torah says the sea split in two. The people walked on a dry path.

check.q: Who took a drum and led the women in dancing?
check.why: The Torah says Miriam took a drum, and the women danced and sang with her.

check.q: Why did the people look back and feel scared?
check.why: The Torah says Pharaoh changed his mind and sent his army after the people.

lessons.title: Telling It Every Year
lessons.mainIdea: Jewish families retell the Exodus story every year at a Passover meal called the Seder.
reading: Every spring, Jewish families sit down for a special meal. It is called the *Seder*. Seder means "order." The meal goes in a set order, step by step.
At the Seder, the youngest child asks four questions. The first is, "Why is this night different?" Then the family tells the story. A baby, a bush, a king, a sea.
There is matzah. There is a bitter herb for the hard years. There is a sweet mix for the bricks. Many Jewish families in Chicago hold a Seder every year.

words.d: the Passover meal where Jewish families tell the Exodus story in order
the small book that tells the story at the Seder; it means "the telling"

look.title: On the Seder Table
rows: Days of Passover in the Torah
look.cite: Exodus (Shemot) 12:15 for seven days; the four questions and four cups from the Passover Haggadah as Jewish tradition keeps it
look.prompt: How many questions does the youngest child ask? Try asking one.

check.q: What does Seder mean?
check.why: Seder means "order." The Passover meal goes step by step.

check.q: Who asks the questions at the Seder?
check.why: At the Seder, the youngest child asks the four questions.

check.q: What is the small book used at the Seder called?
check.why: The Haggadah is the book that tells the story. Its name means "the telling."

review.q: What is the English name for the book Shemot?
review.why: Shemot is the Hebrew name. Exodus is the English name for the same book.

review.q: Who does the Torah say watched the baby's basket?
review.why: Miriam, the baby's big sister, watched the basket in the reeds.

review.q: Where does the Torah say God spoke to Moses?
review.why: The Torah says God spoke to Moses from a bush that burned but did not burn up.

review.q: What did Pharaoh say when Moses asked him to let the people go?
review.why: The Torah says Pharaoh kept saying no. Ten plagues came before he said go.

review.q: Why do Jewish families eat matzah at Passover?
choices: To remember leaving Egypt in a hurry
review.why: Matzah is flat because the bread had no time to rise. It helps families remember.

review.q: What did Miriam do after the people crossed the sea?
choices: She sang and danced with a drum
review.why: The Torah says Miriam took a drum, and the women sang and danced with her.

chapters.title: Mount Sinai and the Ten Sayings
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the Torah say the people heard at the mountain, and how do Jewish families keep those words today?

story.title: One Rule for Our Room
story.kicker: A class writes its own rules, and then hears about a mountain where the Torah says ten sayings were given.
paragraphs: Ms. Ortiz's class sits on the rug. She holds up a big sheet of paper. It is blank. "Today we make rules for our room," she says. "Each of you will write one rule. It should make our room a better place."

Leo writes, "Take turns." Ana writes, "Tell the truth." Jamal writes, "Do not take what is not yours." Priya writes, "Be kind to helpers." Ms. Ortiz tapes each rule to the paper. Soon the paper is full.

"Rules are not just for our room," says Ms. Ortiz. "Long ago, the Torah says, a whole people stood at a mountain. They heard ten sayings. Some of them sound like yours." She reads one: "Honor your father and your mother."

Ana raises her hand. "Do people still keep those rules?" Ms. Ortiz nods. "Jewish families do. They even have a holiday to remember that day. It is called Shavuot." Leo looks at the class rules. "Ours should have a holiday too," he says.
story.think: Which rule would you write for your room? Why would it make the room a better place?

lessons.title: A Camp in the Wilderness
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the people walked to a mountain called Sinai and camped there.
reading: After the sea, the people kept walking. They were in the *wilderness*. That is a wild, dry place with no towns. The Torah says they walked for weeks.
Then they came to a mountain. Its name was Mount *Sinai*. The people set up their tents at the bottom. The whole people camped together.
The Torah says Moses went up the mountain. He came back with a message. The people said, "All that the LORD has spoken, we will do."

words.d: a wild, dry place with no towns; the people walked through it after Egypt
the mountain where the Torah says the people camped and heard the ten sayings

look.title: Counting the Journey
rows: Days of Passover in the Torah
look.cite: Exodus (Shemot) 7–12 and 12:15; Leviticus (Vayikra) 23:15–16, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Which number is on this list two times? Point to it.

check.q: What is a wilderness?
choices: A wild, dry place with no towns
check.why: A wilderness is a wild, dry place. The people walked through it after Egypt.

check.q: Where did the people camp, in the Torah's story?
choices: At the bottom of Mount Sinai
check.why: The Torah says the people set up their tents at the bottom of Mount Sinai.

check.q: Who does the Torah say went up the mountain?
check.why: The Torah says Moses went up Mount Sinai and came back with a message.

lessons.title: Thunder and a Cloud
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says a thick cloud covered the mountain, and the people heard God speak.
reading: The Torah says the people got ready for three days. They washed their clothes. On the third day, there was *thunder*. There was lightning. A thick cloud sat on the mountain.
A loud horn sound grew louder and louder. The people shook. The Torah says God spoke from the mountain. Everyone heard.
Jewish tradition teaches that this is when the *Torah* was given. The story says God gave Moses the teaching to bring to the people.

words.d: the loud boom that comes with a storm; the Torah says thunder came at the mountain
the five books of teaching; Jewish tradition says it was given at Mount Sinai

look.title: Look at the Mountain
look.text: Look at the mountain. A thick gray cloud sits on top. You cannot see the top at all. Lightning flashes inside the cloud. A long horn sound rolls down the mountain. At the bottom, a crowd of people stands very still, holding hands.
look.prompt: How do you think the people at the bottom feel? What would you do if you were there?

check.q: What does the Torah say covered the mountain?
check.why: The Torah says a thick cloud sat on Mount Sinai, with thunder and lightning.

check.q: How many days did the people get ready?
check.why: The Torah says the people got ready for three days before the mountain shook.

check.q: What does Jewish tradition say was given at Mount Sinai?
check.why: Jewish tradition teaches that the Torah, the teaching, was given at Mount Sinai.

lessons.title: One God and a Day of Rest
lessons.mainIdea: The first sayings are about one God and about resting on Shabbat.
reading: Many people call them the Ten Commandments. Jewish tradition calls them the Ten *Sayings*. The first saying starts, "I am the LORD your God." It says God brought the people out of Egypt.
The next sayings say: there is one God. Do not make statues to bow to. Do not use God's name in a bad way.
Then comes *Shabbat*. Remember the seventh day. Rest on that day. Do not work. Jewish families keep this day every week with candles and bread.

words.d: what Jewish tradition calls the Ten Commandments; ten short words to live by
the seventh day, a day of rest; one of the ten sayings is to keep it

look.title: The Shabbat Saying
look.text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
look.prompt: Sabbath is the English word for Shabbat. What does this saying ask people to do?

check.q: What does Jewish tradition call the Ten Commandments?
check.why: Jewish tradition calls them the Ten Sayings. The plagues were in Egypt.

check.q: How does the first saying begin?
choices: I am the LORD your God
check.why: The first saying starts, "I am the LORD your God," and tells of leaving Egypt.

check.q: What does the Shabbat saying ask people to do?
check.why: The saying says to remember the seventh day and rest. Jewish families call it Shabbat.

lessons.title: Family, Truth and What Is Yours
lessons.mainIdea: The other sayings are about how people treat each other.
reading: The first sayings are about God. The rest are about people. The fifth saying is to *honor* your father and your mother. To honor is to treat with care and respect.
Next: do not hurt or kill anyone. Be true to your family. Do not take what is not yours. Do not tell lies about your neighbor.
The last saying is, do not wish for what belongs to someone else. Jewish tradition teaches all ten sayings together. They are about God and about people.

words.d: to treat someone with care and respect; the fifth saying is to honor your parents

look.title: The Fifth Saying
look.text: Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.
look.prompt: "Thy" is an old word for "your." What is one way to honor a parent this week?

check.q: What does honor mean?
choices: To treat with care and respect
check.why: To honor is to treat with care and respect. The fifth saying is to honor your parents.

check.q: Which of these is one of the ten sayings?
choices: Do not take what is not yours
check.why: "Do not take what is not yours" is one of the sayings. The others are not.

check.q: What are the last sayings about?
check.why: The first sayings are about God. The rest are about how people treat each other.

lessons.title: What a Mitzvah Is
lessons.mainIdea: A mitzvah is a commandment in the Torah; Jewish tradition counts many of them.
reading: The ten sayings are not the only rules in the Torah. Each rule is called a *mitzvah*. That means a commandment. Something you are told to do, or not to do.
Some mitzvot are about God. Light candles for Shabbat. Some are about people. Help a person who is poor. Be kind to a stranger. Jewish tradition counts 613 mitzvot in the Torah.
Many Jewish people say "doing a mitzvah" when they do a good deed. Helping a friend carry books is a mitzvah. So is sharing.

words.d: a commandment in the Torah; many Jewish people also use it to mean a good deed

look.title: Counting the Rules
rows: Mitzvot in the Torah, as Jewish tradition counts them
look.cite: Exodus (Shemot) 20; the count of 613 is from the Talmud, Makkot 23b, as Jewish tradition teaches
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? Is 613 more or less than 10?

check.q: What is a mitzvah?
check.why: A mitzvah is a commandment in the Torah. Many people also use it for a good deed.

check.q: How many mitzvot does Jewish tradition count in the Torah?
check.why: Jewish tradition counts 613 mitzvot in the Torah. Ten of them are the sayings.

check.q: Which of these could someone call a mitzvah?
check.why: Helping a friend is a good deed. Many Jewish people call a good deed a mitzvah.

lessons.title: Shavuot: Remembering the Mountain
lessons.mainIdea: Jewish families celebrate Shavuot to remember the day the Torah says the ten sayings were given.
reading: Seven weeks after Passover comes a holiday. It is called *Shavuot*. That means "weeks." Jewish tradition connects this day to Mount Sinai.
On Shavuot, many Jewish families go to the synagogue. They hear the ten sayings read aloud. Many stand up to listen.
Many families eat foods made with milk and cheese. Some decorate with flowers and green plants. Some stay up late to study the Torah. It is a happy day.

words.d: the holiday seven weeks after Passover; Jewish tradition links it to the giving of the Torah

look.title: Two Holidays, One Story
look.text: Look at two tables. The first is a Passover table. There is matzah and a Haggadah. The story is about leaving Egypt. The second is a Shavuot table, seven weeks later. There are flowers and a cheese blintz. The story is about a mountain and ten sayings.
look.prompt: Which table comes first in the year? Which part of the story comes first?

check.q: What does Shavuot mean?
check.why: Shavuot means "weeks." It comes seven weeks after Passover.

check.q: What does Jewish tradition connect Shavuot to?
check.why: Jewish tradition connects Shavuot to the day the Torah was given at Mount Sinai.

check.q: What do many families eat on Shavuot?
check.why: Many Jewish families eat foods made with milk and cheese on Shavuot.

lessons.title: The Torah Scroll in the Synagogue
lessons.mainIdea: In a synagogue, the Torah is a big scroll kept in a special cabinet and read aloud.
reading: A *synagogue* is where Jewish people meet to pray and learn. At the front is a special cabinet. It is called the ark. Inside the ark is the Torah *scroll*.
The scroll is rolled on two wooden poles. It has a cover like a coat. When it is carried, people stand up. A reader uses a little pointer to keep the place.
The words are written in Hebrew by hand. The reader chants them out loud. Each week a new part is read. The whole scroll takes one year.

words.d: the place where Jewish people meet to pray and learn
a long roll of paper or skin; the Torah is written on one

look.title: Look at the Scroll
look.text: Look at the front of the room. The doors of the ark open. Inside stands a tall scroll in a velvet cover. A silver crown sits on top. A person lifts it out. Everyone in the room stands up. The cover comes off. The scroll is rolled open on a table.
look.prompt: Why do you think people stand up when the scroll is carried?

check.q: What is a synagogue?
choices: Where Jewish people meet to pray and learn
check.why: A synagogue is the place where Jewish people meet to pray and learn.

check.q: Where is the Torah scroll kept in the synagogue?
check.why: The Torah scroll is kept in a special cabinet called the ark.

check.q: What do people do when the scroll is carried?
check.why: When the Torah scroll is carried, people in the synagogue stand up.

review.q: What is the name of the mountain in the Torah's story?
review.why: The Torah says the people camped at Mount Sinai and heard the ten sayings there.

review.q: What does Jewish tradition call the Ten Commandments?
review.why: Jewish tradition calls them the Ten Sayings.

review.q: Which saying is about a day of rest?
choices: Do not take what is not yours
review.why: One of the ten sayings is to remember the seventh day, Shabbat, and rest.
A mitzvah is a commandment in the Torah. Many people also use it for a good deed.

review.q: Which holiday comes seven weeks after Passover?
review.why: Shavuot means "weeks." It comes seven weeks after Passover.

review.q: Where is the Torah scroll kept in a synagogue?
review.why: The Torah scroll is kept in the ark, a special cabinet at the front.
